name: Residency and Employment Rights Certificate for Spouse/Civil Partner of a Permanent Resident

qualifying_event.description: The spouse or civil partner of a person holding a Residency and Employment Rights Certificate (permanent residence) may apply for their own Residency and Employment Rights Certificate under the same conditions as the holder (Immigration (Transition) Act, Section 37(16)).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage/civil partnership certificate; proof of the sponsoring spouse's own Residency and Employment Rights Certificate.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires being the spouse or civil partner of a Residency and Employment Rights Certificate holder, applying under the same conditions as the holder.

evidence_required.document: Proof of sponsoring spouse's Residency and Employment Rights Certificate

sources.title: Cayman Islands Immigration (Transition) Act (2022 Revision) -- Section 37(16): spouse/civil partner of a Residency and Employment Rights Certificate holder may apply for their own certificate under the same conditions; Section 37(18): surviving spouse/partner may reapply within 3 months after the holder's death

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the Cayman Islands' initial build. Modelled separately from ky_permanent_residence_general.json because Section 37(16) gives the spouse an independently-held certificate (their own status, not derivative dependant status), distinct from simply being listed as a dependant on the primary holder's certificate. work_rights follows the same 'restricted' logic as the underlying RERC (occupation-specified, not unrestricted). Section 37(18) additionally provides that if the primary certificate holder dies, the surviving spouse/civil partner's right to reside may be revoked at Board/Director discretion, but the survivor may reapply within 3 months for their own Residency and Employment Rights Certificate -- this is a meaningful protection not modelled as its own separate route but flagged here since it materially affects what happens to this status on the sponsor's death. switchable_to points to ky_caymanian_status_marriage.json, since a spouse holding Cayman residence in this way is a plausible route into the marriage-based Caymanian-status grounds under Section 28(5).
